claim.quote: The DAMA/LIBRA-phase1 data give evidence for the presence of Dark Matter (DM) particles in the galactic halo, on the basis of the exploited model independent DM annual modulation signature by using highly radio-pure NaI(Tl) target, at 7.5 sigma C.L..

key_value.quote: The results obtained with the total exposure of 1.04 ton x yr collected by DAMA/LIBRA-phase1

name: Final model independent result of DAMA/LIBRA-phase1

significance.value: 7.5 sigma C.L. (DAMA/LIBRA-phase1); 9.3 sigma C.L. including DAMA/NaI

summary.plain: The final DAMA/LIBRA-phase1 result: seven years of data in which, the team says, the detector's rate varies through the year as dark matter would make it, at 7.5 standard deviations (9.3 with DAMA/NaI added).
summary.technical: Total exposure 1.04 ton yr over 7 annual cycles; with DAMA/NaI (cumulative 1.33 ton yr, 14 annual cycles) the C.L. is 9.3 sigma; amplitude (0.0112 +- 0.0012) cpd/kg/keV (2-6 keV), phase (144 +- 7) d, period (0.998 +- 0.002) yr; the abstract adds that no systematic or side reaction able to mimic the signature has been found or suggested by anyone over more than a decade.

title: Final model independent result of DAMA/LIBRA-phase1
why_it_matters: Closes the first phase of DAMA/LIBRA before the 2010 upgrade; the abstract uses the word 'evidence'.
